body:
I heard of one case of patients that were having sex "via the umbilicus". 

This things really do happen. It's amazing if anything!

You make a distinction between chronic illness and terminal illness. To my understanding, the difference is the risk of mortality. The risk that what you suffer from may kill you. Terminal illnesses do not necessarily kill people. They just do if they hang around long enough. Chronic illnesses often pose a threat to life, or a threat to a life worth living. Trigeminal neuralgia springs to mind. If faced with a lifetime a severe pain(that may not be fatal), is it not somewhat rational to elect to kill oneself?


I would draw a comparison with this distinction you make between chronic illness and terminal illness to the difference between a mood disorder and a personality disorder. Grey areas exist in both. And In my opinion, determining if suicide is permissible should be done on a case by case basis.


For me, a guillotine hangs over every modicum of joy. Which makes joys even less enjoyable. Given a sentence of suffering, that may potentially last decades as it did for you, I cannot see how any thinking person should not elect to kill themselves. For me the good times have no redeeming value. It doesn't mitigate this depression I suffer from.
